title: Freight GHG emissions report
statement: Calculated with Sootcase following the GLEC Framework v3.3 and ISO 14083:2023 methodology. Conformity with ISO 14083 is not declared by this report.
reference: Per-shipment results with factors, sources and distances: Sootcase batch output for the same input. Method: https://github.com/majidkabir/sootcase

default_sources.source: GLEC Framework v3.3 (Smart Freight Centre, 2026), Section 3 Module 2, Tables 18-19, container vessels (Clean Cargo trade lane factors, reporting year 2025): industry average (origin-destination pair unknown), dry, 13 + 60.4 g CO2e/TEU-km (WTT + TTW) / 10 t per TEU (GLEC's average when the cargo mass is not known); includes GLEC's +15% distance conversion, so it is per shortest feasible distance

GLEC Framework v3.3 (Smart Freight Centre, 2026), Section 3 Module 2, Table 3, logistics hubs (GILA project: Fraunhofer IML, Politecnico di Milano, GreenRouter; median values): warehouse, ambient (n = 92)

GLEC Framework v3.3 (Smart Freight Centre, 2026), Section 3 Module 2, road, temperature-controlled: glec/road/eu_sa/rigid_26_32t/diesel with GLEC's +12% uplift for temperature-controlled vehicles over 3.5 t GVW (p. 106; given for Europe, South America, Asia and Africa); includes GLEC's +5% distance conversion, so it is per shortest feasible distance

GLEC Framework v3.3 (Smart Freight Centre, 2026), Section 3 Module 2, Table 3, logistics hubs (GILA project; market study by EcoTransIT World 2025, conducted and updated by SGKV and Fraunhofer IML 2026): intermodal terminals (sea and inland ports), ambient (n = 84), 18.2 kg CO2e per container

models.model: Energy-based model: electricity per tonne-km times the country's grid intensity
Activity-based load model: per vehicle-km emissions interpolated between 0%, 50% and 100% laden, payload derived from the dataset (see the dataset's load_models)

distance_adjustments.source: GLEC Framework v3.3 (Smart Freight Centre, 2026), Section 1 Chapter 4 (road): when the emission intensity is based on actual distance, a DAF must be applied; 5% as in GLEC's own road default values (Section 3 Module 2), which include a +5% distance conversion between actual and shortest feasible distance

notes: Hub emissions are reported well-to-wheel only: the hub factors used carry no split into operational and energy provision emissions. Operational (TTW) and energy provision (WTT) totals therefore cover transport only.
For 2.6% of tonne-km the type of distance was not stated (distances given without distance_type).
Tonne-km combine more than one type of distance; see the shares per mode.
Where a leg's distance type differed from the basis of its emission intensity, a distance adjustment factor was applied; these are listed with their sources.
Default emission intensities are used where no primary data (measured fuel or operation category values) was supplied for a leg or hub; their sources are listed.

factor.source: 0.08 kWh/tkm x DNK grid 114.41 g/kWh (2025, Ember via Our World in Data: Denmark)

legs.factor_note: "diesel": no country known for the leg's ends, so glec/fuel/eu/diesel/l.

fuel_factor.source: GLEC Framework v3.3 (Smart Freight Centre, 2026), Section 3 Module 1, GHG emission factors: European sources (pp. 77-78; ifeu, infras & Fraunhofer IML 2025): diesel, 3.22 kg CO2e/kg TTW, 4.19 kg CO2e/kg WTW, × 0.83 kg/l (GLEC's density) per litre

legs.daf_source: GLEC Framework v3.3 (Smart Freight Centre, 2026), Section 1 Chapter 4 (road): when the emission intensity is based on actual distance, a DAF must be applied; 5% as in GLEC's own road default values (Section 3 Module 2), which include a +5% distance conversion between actual and shortest feasible distance

factor.source: load model (load 16 t, 90% of the model's payload, empty trip factor 0, payload 17.8 t) from DESNZ 2026: Freighting goods > HGV (non-refrigerated, all diesel) > Average non-refrigerated artics (per km at 0/50/100% laden; payload from 100% laden per tonne.km)

legs.factor_note: Cargo type "container": the dataset has no value for it with glec/sea/container/industry_average/dry, so that vehicle's own value is used.

factor.source: GLEC Framework v3.3 (Smart Freight Centre, 2026), Section 3 Module 2, Tables 18-19, container vessels (Clean Cargo trade lane factors, reporting year 2025): industry average (origin-destination pair unknown), dry, 13 + 60.4 g CO2e/TEU-km (WTT + TTW) / 10 t per TEU (GLEC's average when the cargo mass is not known); includes GLEC's +15% distance conversion, so it is per shortest feasible distance

hubs.note: Cargo type "container": the dataset has no value for it at a intermodal_terminal hub, so that hub type's own value is used.
hubs.source: GLEC Framework v3.3 (Smart Freight Centre, 2026), Section 3 Module 2, Table 3, logistics hubs (GILA project; market study by EcoTransIT World 2025, conducted and updated by SGKV and Fraunhofer IML 2026): intermodal terminals (sea and inland ports), ambient (n = 84), 18.2 kg CO2e per container

factor.source: GLEC Framework v3.3 (Smart Freight Centre, 2026), Section 3 Module 2, road, temperature-controlled: glec/road/eu_sa/rigid_26_32t/diesel with GLEC's +12% uplift for temperature-controlled vehicles over 3.5 t GVW (p. 106; given for Europe, South America, Asia and Africa); includes GLEC's +5% distance conversion, so it is per shortest feasible distance

hubs.note: Cargo type "temperature_controlled": the dataset has no value for it at a warehouse hub, so that hub type's own value is used.
hubs.source: GLEC Framework v3.3 (Smart Freight Centre, 2026), Section 3 Module 2, Table 3, logistics hubs (GILA project: Fraunhofer IML, Politecnico di Milano, GreenRouter; median values): warehouse, ambient (n = 92)
